title: Sidon Set
content: A **Sidon set** (B₂ sequence) is a set where all pairwise sums $a + b$ with $a \le b$ are distinct. Equivalently: $a + b = c + d$ with $a \le b$ and $c \le d$ implies $a = c$ and $b = d$. Named after Simon Sidon who studied these in the context of Fourier series and lacunary sets.
mathContext: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is Sidon if $a + b = c + d$ with $a \le b$, $c \le d$, and $a, b, c, d \in A$ implies $(a, b) = (c, d)$. Equivalently, the representation function $r(n) = |\{(a,b) \in A^2 : a \le b,\, a + b = n\}| \le 1$ for all $n$.

title: Distinct Sums Characterization
content: Alternative definition without the ordering constraint: $a + b = c + d$ implies $\{a,b\} = \{c,d\}$ as unordered pairs. This symmetric formulation is often more natural in proofs since it avoids case splits on orderings.
mathContext: $\text{HasDistinctSums}(A) :\Leftrightarrow \forall a,b,c,d \in A,\; a+b = c+d \Rightarrow \{a,b\} = \{c,d\}$. This is equivalent to saying the sumset $A + A$ has maximal size $\binom{|A|+1}{2}$.

title: Equivalence of Definitions
content: The two Sidon definitions (ordered and unordered) are equivalent. The forward direction deduces unordered equality from ordered equality by case-splitting on whether $a \le b$ and $c \le d$. The reverse applies the ordering constraints to eliminate the swapped case. This is fully proved without axioms.
mathContext: $\text{IsSidonSet}(A) \Leftrightarrow \text{HasDistinctSums}(A)$. The proof handles four cases from the two independent orderings $(a \le b \text{ or } a > b)$ and $(c \le d \text{ or } c > d)$, using `omega` for arithmetic.

title: Sidon Number h(N)
content: The Sidon number $h(N)$ is the maximum cardinality of a Sidon set contained in $\{1, \ldots, N\}$. This is the central quantity in the Erdős-Turán conjecture: understanding the precise growth rate of $h(N)$ as $N \to \infty$.
mathContext: $h(N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq \{0, \ldots, N\},\, A \text{ is Sidon}\}$. It is known that $h(N) = N^{1/2} + \Theta(N^{1/4})$ with the conjecture asking if the $N^{1/4}$ can be replaced by $N^\varepsilon$.

title: Sidon Sets Exist
content: A simple existence proof: the empty set is trivially a Sidon set since the condition is vacuously true. This ensures $h(N) \ge 0$ and that the supremum in the definition of $h(N)$ is taken over a nonempty family.
mathContext: The proof witnesses $A = \emptyset$, which satisfies $\text{IsSidonSet}(\emptyset)$ vacuously: there are no $a, b, c, d \in \emptyset$ to violate the condition.

title: Erdős Problem #30 (OPEN)
content: The main conjecture with a \$1,000 prize: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = N^{1/2} + O_\varepsilon(N^\varepsilon)$. This asks whether the error term between $h(N)$ and $\sqrt{N}$ can be made smaller than any fixed polynomial. The N^{1/4} barrier has resisted all attacks since 1941.
mathContext: $\text{Erdos30Conjecture} :\Leftrightarrow \forall \varepsilon > 0,\; \exists C_\varepsilon > 0,\; \exists N_0,\; \forall N \ge N_0,\; |h(N) - \sqrt{N}| \le C_\varepsilon \cdot N^\varepsilon$. This is stronger than just an upper bound — it also controls fluctuations below $\sqrt{N}$.

title: Stronger Conjecture: O(1) Error
content: Erdős's 'optimistic' conjecture: $h(N) = N^{1/2} + O(1)$, meaning the deviation from $\sqrt{N}$ is bounded by an absolute constant. Even Erdős considered this 'possibly too optimistic' but computations for small $N$ are consistent with it.
mathContext: $\text{StrongerConjecture} :\Leftrightarrow \exists C > 0,\; \forall N,\; |h(N) - \sqrt{N}| \le C$. If true, this would imply the main conjecture trivially since $C \le C \cdot N^\varepsilon$ for $N \ge 1$.

title: Erdős-Turán Upper Bound (1941)
content: The foundational upper bound: $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + N^{1/4} + 1$. Proved by a counting argument: in a Sidon set of size $s$, there are $\binom{s}{2}$ distinct pairwise sums, all at most $2N$, giving $\binom{s}{2} \le 2N$, whence $s \le N^{1/2} + N^{1/4} + 1$.
mathContext: The proof counts: $|A| = s$ gives $\binom{s}{2}$ distinct sums in $\{2, \ldots, 2N\}$, so $s(s-1)/2 \le 2N-1$, yielding $s \le \frac{1 + \sqrt{1 + 4(2N-1)}}{2} \le \sqrt{N} + N^{1/4} + 1$.

title: Lindström's Improvement (1969)
content: A minor refinement: $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + N^{1/4} + 1/2$. Lindström improved the constant term by a more careful analysis of the Erdős-Turán counting argument, but the $N^{1/4}$ exponent remained unchanged.
mathContext: Lindström tightened the inequality to $s(s-1)/2 \le N$ (instead of $2N-1$) by noting that both $a+b$ and $c+d$ must be in $\{2, \ldots, 2N\}$ and using parity considerations.

title: Balogh-Füredi-Roy Breakthrough (2021)
content: The first improvement to the $N^{1/4}$ coefficient in 80 years: $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + 0.998 \cdot N^{1/4}$. While the improvement is numerically small, it broke a long-standing psychological barrier and introduced new graph-theoretic techniques to the problem.
mathContext: The coefficient improved from $1$ to $0.998$, saving $0.002 \cdot N^{1/4}$ elements. The proof uses the structure of the 'collision graph' where vertices are elements and edges connect pairs with equal sums.

title: Carter-Hunter-O'Bryant (2025)
content: Current state-of-the-art: $h(N) \le N^{1/2} + 0.98183 \cdot N^{1/4} + O(1)$. This further refined the Balogh-Füredi-Roy approach, but the exponent $1/4$ itself remains untouched — all improvements since 1941 have only affected the constant multiplier.
mathContext: The bound $h(N) \le \sqrt{N} + 0.98183 \cdot N^{1/4} + C$ for some absolute constant $C$. The gap from $0.998$ to $0.98183$ represents continued optimization of the collision-counting framework.

title: Singer's Lower Bound (1938)
content: The asymptotically optimal lower bound: $h(N) \ge (1 - o(1)) \sqrt{N}$. Singer's construction uses perfect difference sets arising from the action of $\text{PGL}(2, \mathbb{F}_q)$ on the projective plane $\text{PG}(2, q)$, giving Sidon sets of size $q+1$ in $\{0, \ldots, q^2+q\}$ for prime powers $q$.
mathContext: For every $\varepsilon > 0$ and sufficiently large $N$, $h(N) \ge (1-\varepsilon)\sqrt{N}$. Since $h(N) \le \sqrt{N} + O(N^{1/4})$, this means $h(N)/\sqrt{N} \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$.

title: Explicit Lower Bound
content: For infinitely many $N$: $h(N) \ge N^{1/2} - N^{0.525}$. This quantitative version of Singer's bound shows the error term on the lower side is smaller than $N^{1/4}$, though it only holds along a subsequence (where $N$ is near a prime-squared).
mathContext: The exponent $0.525$ in the error term comes from gaps between consecutive primes: if $p$ is the largest prime with $p^2 + p + 1 \le N$, then $N - (p^2+p+1) = O(N^{0.525})$ by the Baker-Harman-Pintz bound on prime gaps.

title: Required Upper Bound and Reduction
content: Formalizes what proving the conjecture requires: an upper bound with exponent $\varepsilon < 1/4$. The metastatement `conjecture_from_small_epsilon` captures the key structural insight that any single improvement to an exponent below $1/4$ would imply the full conjecture, since $N^{\varepsilon_0} \le N^\varepsilon$ for large $N$ when $\varepsilon > \varepsilon_0$.
mathContext: $\text{RequiredUpperBound}(\varepsilon) :\Leftrightarrow \exists C > 0,\; \forall N \ge 1,\; h(N) \le \sqrt{N} + C \cdot N^\varepsilon$. The axiom states: $(\exists \varepsilon \in (0, 1/4),\; \text{RequiredUpperBound}(\varepsilon)) \Rightarrow \text{Erdos30Conjecture}$.

title: Perfect Difference Set
content: A set $D \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ where every non-zero residue appears exactly once as a difference $d_1 - d_2$ with $d_1, d_2 \in D$. These exist whenever $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for a prime power $q$, arising from lines in the projective plane $\text{PG}(2, q)$.
mathContext: From finite projective planes: the Singer cycle in $\text{PGL}(3, \mathbb{F}_q)$ acts transitively on lines of $\text{PG}(2,q)$. A line has $q+1$ points, and the orbit gives a perfect difference set of size $q+1$ modulo $q^2+q+1$.

title: Perfect Difference Sets are Sidon
content:
Every perfect difference set is automatically a Sidon set. If $a + b = c + d$ with $\{a,b\} 
e \{c,d\}$, then $a - c = d - b 
e 0$ and $a - d = c - b 
e 0$ give two representations of the same nonzero difference, contradicting the 'exactly once' property.
mathContext: The uniqueness condition on differences implies the Sidon condition: $r_2(n) \le 1$ for all $n$, where $r_2(n) = |\{(a,b) \in D^2 : a-b = n\}|$. Since $a+b = c+d \Leftrightarrow a-c = d-b$, having distinct representations of sums gives distinct representations of differences.

title: Singer's Construction
content: For any prime power $q$, there exists a perfect difference set of size $q+1$ modulo $q^2 + q + 1$. This gives Sidon sets of size approximately $\sqrt{N}$ for infinitely many $N$, establishing the lower bound $h(N) \ge (1-o(1))\sqrt{N}$.
mathContext: Singer (1938) showed: fix a generator $g$ of the cyclic group $(\mathbb{F}_{q^3})^*/\mathbb{F}_q^*$ of order $q^2+q+1$. The set $D = \{i : g^i \in \text{some fixed line}\}$ is a perfect difference set of size $q+1$.

title: Example: {1, 2, 5, 10} is Sidon
content: A concrete verified example: $\{1, 2, 5, 10\}$ is a Sidon set with pairwise sums $3, 6, 7, 11, 12, 15$ — all distinct. The proof uses exhaustive case analysis with `omega` to verify all $\binom{4}{2}^2 = 36$ equality conditions.
